fields.name: How to Set Up a Cloud Kitchen in India: The Ultimate Checklist
fields.description:
Cloud kitchens are transforming how food businesses operate in India. With no dine-in setup and a delivery-first model, they allow entrepreneurs to enter the market with lower investment and operational costs. However, success depends on much more than just a good recipe—it requires careful planning, licenses, the right technology, and a strong marketing strategy.

In this blog, we break down the step-by-step checklist to set up a cloud kitchen in India, helping you move from idea to execution with clarity and confidence.

Choose the Right Location for Your Cloud Kitchen

Unlike restaurants, cloud kitchens don’t depend on customer footfall or ambiance. However, the right location still plays a critical role in determining your reach and order volume.

High-demand delivery zones: Your cloud kitchen should be located in a delivery hotspot. This means areas with a high density of residential complexes, office hubs, or colleges where online food ordering is frequent. Use data from platforms like Swiggy, Zomato, or Google Trends to understand cuisine demand in your target area. The goal is to be close to your customers to ensure faster deliveries and higher order volumes.

Basic infrastructure availability: Don’t overlook basics like electricity, water supply, drainage, and sanitation. Your kitchen operations—from cooking to cleaning—depend on these essentials. Interruptions in power or water can cause serious service delays and lead to health and safety issues. Confirm that the site has provisions for exhausts, waste disposal, and ventilation before signing a lease.

Low rentals: A key advantage of cloud kitchens is their ability to function without high-street visibility. This allows you to avoid premium commercial rents. Choose industrial or secondary commercial areas where real estate is more affordable. Make sure the cost savings don’t come at the expense of poor access or unreliable utilities.

Rider accessibility: Your location should make pickups fast and hassle-free. Delivery executives from Swiggy or Zomato should be able to enter, collect the order, and exit quickly—especially during peak hours. Properties with ground floor access, clear signage, and a designated pickup counter tend to be most efficient.

No dine-in requirement: Since you're not serving walk-in customers, you can skip investing in decor, furniture, or parking space. Instead, focus on a clean, compact, and functional kitchen layout. You only need enough room for your staff, equipment, inventory, and packing station.

Get All Required Licenses and Registrations

Legal compliance is not just mandatory—it builds trust with delivery aggregators and consumers, and ensures your business can run smoothly without risk of fines or shutdowns.

FSSAI License: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) license confirms your kitchen meets national food safety standards. It’s mandatory for all food businesses and essential to list your brand on any aggregator. The application process involves submitting your business plan, kitchen layout, and food categories. Validity ranges from 1 to 5 years.

GST Registration: If your annual turnover exceeds ₹20 lakhs, GST registration is legally required. It allows you to issue invoices with tax, claim input credits, and operate on platforms that require GST-compliant billing. Even if you’re under the limit, registering early prepares your brand for scalability.

Municipal Health Trade License: Issued by your local municipal authority, this license confirms your facility maintains public health norms. Expect an inspection focusing on cleanliness, waste management, and kitchen hygiene before approval is granted.

Shop & Establishment Act Registration:
This license legally registers your cloud kitchen as a commercial business entity under labor laws. It’s needed to open business bank accounts, sign vendor contracts, and hire staff legally.

Fire & Safety License: If your kitchen uses LPG or open flame equipment, you must comply with fire safety norms. This includes installing fire extinguishers, smoke detectors, and having a clear evacuation plan. Authorities may conduct inspections before granting this license.

PFA Act Clearance Certificate: The Prevention of Food Adulteration (PFA) Act ensures your kitchen avoids any harmful food practices. This certificate is essential if you’re preparing foods using raw materials or doing your own packaging.

Pollution Certificate & Environmental Clearance: Some locations require these certificates, especially if your kitchen generates significant waste, noise, or emissions. Compliance ensures you don’t face legal action from environmental boards.

Eating House License: In some states or cities, even cloud kitchens need an Eating House License if they operate from shared kitchen spaces or commissary models. Check your local laws to confirm whether it's required.

Set Up Key Amenities for Daily Operations

Your kitchen’s layout and infrastructure must be built for efficiency, safety, and compliance. Even minor oversights can slow operations or lead to fines.

Hygienic storage area: Divide your storage into clear sections—dry goods, perishables, frozen items, and packaging. Use stainless steel racks, food-safe containers, and well-labeled bins to avoid cross-contamination. Implement a FIFO (First In, First Out) system to maintain freshness and minimize waste.

Ventilation and chimneys: Install a commercial-grade exhaust system to remove heat, steam, and airborne grease. This keeps your staff safe and comfortable while preventing damage to equipment. Good ventilation also helps meet fire and health codes.

24/7 electricity with backup: Your ovens, refrigerators, and POS systems all require continuous power. Even a short outage during rush hour can impact dozens of orders. Invest in inverters or backup generators to avoid costly downtime.

Drainage system: Install floor drains with anti-clog covers and slope the floor properly to prevent water accumulation. Schedule regular cleaning to prevent pest infestation and ensure hygiene compliance during inspections.

Reliable water supply: You’ll need water for food prep, cleaning, and sanitation throughout the day. Consider installing a water filter or RO system to ensure purity. Backup water storage tanks can also help during shortages.

Invest in Commercial Kitchen Equipment, Raw Materials & Packaging

Investing in the right equipment and supplies is non-negotiable when you want consistency and efficiency in your kitchen operations.

Kitchen appliances: Choose appliances suited to your menu. For example, if you're making pizzas, invest in a deck oven; for North Indian food, you'll need a tandoor and hotplates. Energy-efficient appliances can reduce your operating costs in the long run.

High-quality raw materials: Source fresh ingredients from certified vendors. Build relationships with two or more suppliers to avoid stock disruptions. Use digital inventory tracking to monitor consumption and reduce wastage.

Effective packaging solutions: Your packaging should keep the food intact, hot, and presentable even after a 30–40 minute delivery journey. Use tamper-proof seals for safety, and choose container designs that fit your food types—ventilated boxes for fried foods, insulated bowls for curries, etc. Add your branding for a professional touch.

Use Technology to Streamline Operations

A tech-enabled setup gives cloud kitchens the agility to scale and respond to customer needs in real time.

Food aggregator integration: Sign up on platforms like Swiggy, Zomato, and ONDC. Optimize your listings with sharp images, keyword-rich descriptions, and competitive pricing. Stay responsive to reviews and use aggregator dashboards to analyze peak times and bestsellers.

POS system: Choose a POS that integrates with your aggregator accounts and supports real-time KOT printing, inventory tracking, customer order history, and tax reporting. A cloud-based POS also allows remote access for monitoring and decision-making.

Internet and telecom: Your kitchen should have a stable broadband connection to avoid delays in receiving orders. A dedicated business phone number helps you manage customer calls and partner communication efficiently.

Security systems: Install high-definition CCTV cameras in prep, storage, and packaging zones. This ensures quality control, reduces wastage, and helps resolve customer complaints related to missing items or order tampering.

Hire the Right Team for Your Cloud Kitchen

Even with a delivery-only model, having the right team is crucial for kitchen efficiency and food quality.

Chefs: Hire chefs who can handle high-pressure environments and repetitive batch cooking without compromising quality. Their experience with standardized recipes and time management is critical for consistent delivery.

Kitchen helpers: They handle washing, chopping, cleaning, and restocking—freeing chefs to focus on cooking. Helpers are the backbone of smooth kitchen operations, especially during peak times.

Housekeeper: Cleanliness is non-negotiable. A dedicated cleaner ensures that your kitchen, storage, and rest areas are spotless. This is important for daily operations as well as hygiene audits.

Delivery staff (optional): In-house delivery agents can give you more control over service quality, timing, and customer interaction. Use branded uniforms and delivery bags to maintain a professional appearance.

Market Your Cloud Kitchen Effectively

Digital visibility is everything for a cloud kitchen. A well-planned marketing strategy is the key to consistent order flow and long-term brand building.

Google My Business: Your GMB listing acts like a storefront online. Add location, menu links, phone number, and high-quality photos. Encourage reviews from satisfied customers to improve your local ranking.

Social media presence: Build your brand through engaging content on Instagram, Facebook, and even YouTube. Share food photography, behind-the-scenes videos, and limited-time offers to drive curiosity and loyalty.

fields.name: How to Set Up a Commercial Bakery in India: The Ultimate Checklist
fields.description:
Dreaming of the aroma of fresh bread and pastries filling your own bakery? Setting up a commercial bakery in India is an exciting venture — but it requires thoughtful planning, the right resources, and a smart strategy to ensure lasting success. Whether you aim to welcome walk-in customers or deliver sweet delights through online food apps, this complete guide will walk you through everything you need to know about how to set up a commercial bakery in India.

Choose the Right Location for Your Bakery

Finding the ideal location is the cornerstone of a thriving bakery. A good spot not only attracts customers but also ensures daily operations run without hiccups.

Space: Make sure your bakery has a well-designed kitchen with ample room for baking stations, storage racks, and essential appliances. Cramped kitchens can slow down production and compromise food safety. If you plan to offer dine-in services, allocate space for a clean, comfortable seating area. A well-thought-out layout keeps workflow smooth and staff stress-free.

Connectivity: Location accessibility is vital. Choose a place that is easy to reach via main roads and public transport. Busy commercial zones near schools, offices, and residential complexes tend to have higher footfall, which can significantly boost daily sales.

Utilities: Always verify that the location has reliable water and electricity connections. Baking equipment such as ovens, chillers, and mixers require steady power supply to maintain product quality and avoid downtime.

Rental Considerations: Unlike full-scale restaurants, bakeries can thrive in modest spaces if you focus on takeaways and deliveries. This not only reduces high rental costs but also makes your business lean and profitable.

Get All Required Licenses and Registrations

Running a bakery without proper licenses can lead to heavy fines or closure. Securing these legal permits safeguards your business and builds trust with customers.

GST Registration: If your bakery’s annual revenue exceeds Rs 20 lakhs, registering for GST is mandatory. It allows you to legally charge and collect taxes, making your financial records compliant and transparent.

FSSAI License: This license from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ensures that the food you serve meets safety and hygiene norms. It’s a must-have for gaining customer confidence. The process is simple and costs around Rs 5,000.

Trademark Registration: Protect your unique brand name, logo, and signature recipes by registering a trademark. This legal safeguard prevents other businesses from imitating your branding or menu, ensuring your identity stays exclusive.

Fire Safety License: After setting up necessary fire safety measures like extinguishers and alarms, get your fire license from the local fire department. It’s not just a legal formality but a critical step to keep your staff and customers safe.

Eating House License: If your bakery includes seating where customers can eat on-site, you’ll need this license from the city or state police. It certifies that your premises comply with public safety standards.

Health License: Issued by the municipal health department, this license confirms that your bakery maintains the required health and hygiene standards. It usually costs around Rs 3,000 and should be renewed periodically.

Essential Equipment Needed for a Commercial Bakery

The right equipment sets the stage for smooth production and consistent product quality. Think of it as the backbone of your bakery’s daily operations.

Stainless Steel (SS) Tray Trolley & Storage Racks: These help organize trays of dough, baked goods, and raw ingredients efficiently. Stainless steel is durable, rust-resistant, and easy to clean — which is crucial in a food environment.

SS Sink: A sturdy, easy-to-clean sink is vital for washing utensils, cleaning ingredients, and maintaining overall hygiene in the kitchen. Proper cleaning stations help prevent cross-contamination and foodborne illnesses.

Display Showcase: A well-lit display counter — both refrigerated for cakes and desserts, and heated for savories — entices customers and boosts impulse buys. An attractive showcase turns your baked goods into eye-catching treats.

Commercial Chiller: A heavy-duty chiller keeps perishables like fresh cream, butter, and fruits at the right temperature, extending shelf life and reducing waste.

Dough Proofer & Mixer: High-capacity proofers and mixers are time-savers that ensure your dough rises perfectly every time and your batters are mixed consistently, maintaining product quality across batches.

High-Quality Oven: Your oven is the heart of your bakery. Invest in one that suits your menu volume and type — whether it’s deck, convection, or rotary. A reliable oven ensures even baking and helps you meet large orders on time.

Hire Skilled Staff for Your Bakery

A passionate, skilled team is the secret ingredient behind every successful bakery. Each staff member plays a vital role in keeping operations smooth and customers happy.

Head Chef: The head chef oversees recipe development, quality control, and final presentation. They ensure that every item — from cookies to elaborate cakes — maintains consistent taste and appearance.

Commi Level Chef: These chefs assist in preparing batters, mixing dough, baking, decorating pastries, and handling everyday prep work. Their hands-on support helps maintain production flow during busy hours.

Cashier: A friendly, efficient cashier handles billing, processes online and in-store orders, and is often the first point of contact for customers. Their good communication skills can enhance customer experience and encourage repeat visits.

Service Boys: Service staff are responsible for serving dine-in customers, packing takeaway orders neatly, and ensuring the front area is clean and welcoming at all times.

Helpers: Kitchen helpers manage ingredient prepping, dishwashing, cleaning, and basic maintenance tasks, allowing chefs to focus entirely on baking and decorating.

Must-Have Amenities for Smooth Bakery Operations

Providing the right amenities is essential for a clean, comfortable, and productive work environment — for both staff and customers.

Seating & Hygiene: If your bakery has tables and chairs, maintain them to high standards of cleanliness and comfort. A pleasant seating area can encourage customers to stay longer and order more.

Restrooms: A hygienic restroom for staff is non-negotiable. It boosts morale and complies with labor regulations, showing that you care about your team’s well-being.

Storage Space: Designate a separate, organized storage zone for raw materials, packaging supplies, and finished products. Proper storage minimizes spoilage and keeps your kitchen clutter-free.

Ventilation: Good airflow is vital in a bakery, where ovens generate significant heat. Proper ventilation keeps the workspace cool, reduces odors, and maintains a fresh environment.

Order Placement Area: A well-designed counter area allows multiple customers to place orders comfortably, especially during peak times. Ensure it is spacious and tidy to make a great first impression.

Use Technology to Streamline Operations 

Smart use of technology can help you manage orders efficiently, maintain security, and scale your business.

Security Cameras: Installing CCTV cameras protects your premises, deters theft, and gives you peace of mind when you’re away. It also helps monitor staff performance and customer flow.

Smartphone for Orders: A dedicated business phone ensures you never miss an order notification from Zomato, Swiggy, or WhatsApp. It’s a simple tool that keeps you connected with your customers 24/7.

POS System: A robust Point of Sale system handles billing, tracks daily sales, manages inventory, and generates detailed reports. This makes it easier to spot trends, manage stock, and plan promotions.

Effective Marketing Strategies to Promote Your Bakery

Your delicious products need to reach as many people as possible. A smart marketing plan ensures that your bakery stands out in a competitive market.

Google Business Profile: List your bakery on Google to appear in local searches and on Google Maps. Regularly update it with photos, menu items, operating hours, and customer reviews to increase foot traffic.

Food Delivery Platforms: Register on popular platforms like Zomato and Swiggy to tap into the growing online delivery market. Well-maintained listings with attractive photos and good ratings can drive substantial online sales.

Paid Ads: Running targeted ads on Google and social media can quickly attract new customers in your locality. Promotions, discounts, and special deals often work well for bakeries.

Social Media Marketing: Engage your audience on Instagram and Facebook by posting mouth-watering photos, videos, behind-the-scenes content, and customer testimonials. Creative posts and regular updates build a loyal community around your brand.

Setting up a commercial bakery in India is an adventure filled with sweet opportunities and learning curves. With smart planning, the right equipment, skilled staff, and effective marketing, your bakery can win hearts and build a loyal customer base.

Wishing you delicious success and happy baking!

fields.name: How to Choose the Right Outlet Type for Your F&B Business in India: A Complete Guide
fields.description:
Choosing the right format for your food and beverage (F&B) business can define your success—or struggle. Whether you're opening a high-end full-service restaurant or launching a delivery-only cloud kitchen, the outlet type you choose impacts your investment, operations, and growth potential.

In this detailed guide, we’ll explore the four main outlet types—Full-Service Restaurant, Café, Cloud Kitchen, and Quick Service Restaurant (QSR)—along with the pros, cons, estimated investment, and who they’re best suited for. If you're a first-time founder or expanding an existing brand, this guide will help you make an informed, profitable decision.

Full-Service Restaurant: 

A full-service restaurant (FSR) is a traditional dine-in format where guests are seated, attended to by servers, and offered a full-course meal. This model focuses on providing an immersive experience that combines ambience, hospitality, and cuisine.

Why Choose a Full-Service Restaurant?

You should consider launching a full-service restaurant if your brand vision revolves around creating a high-end dining experience that customers can’t get at home or from delivery. FSRs are perfect for chef-led concepts, experiential cuisine, and ambience-driven brands. If your menu is premium and you want customers to associate your brand with quality, exclusivity, or indulgence, this format lets you control every touchpoint—from plate presentation to lighting and service.

This format also offers the best opportunity for storytelling. Through interiors, music, lighting, and tableware, you can build a strong brand personality. Think of fine-dining spots like Olive Bar & Kitchen or restaurants like Bastian and Bombay Canteen, which are as famous for their vibe as they are for their food.

Pros & Cons of Full-Service Restaurants:

One of the biggest advantages is the ability to create a premium customer experience that justifies higher pricing. The average bill value (ABV) is significantly higher than in other formats, giving you a chance to earn more per customer. You can also up-sell alcoholic beverages, desserts, and add-ons—something that's more challenging in delivery-first or casual formats.

Another benefit is brand loyalty. People form emotional connections with dine-in experiences, which can lead to repeat visits, word-of-mouth marketing, and long-term profitability.

However, the downside is the high capital investment required. A full-service restaurant in a prime area can easily cost upwards of ₹50 lakhs, sometimes reaching ₹1 crore or more. You’ll need to invest in interiors, kitchen infrastructure, service staff, licenses, and marketing.

Operationally, FSRs are complex. Managing service quality, table turnover, kitchen timing, and guest feedback all require strong systems and experienced staff. Additionally, break-even periods can stretch beyond 18–24 months, depending on location and pricing strategy.

Café: 

A café is a casual food and beverage outlet that primarily serves coffee, tea, snacks, and small meals. It typically focuses on comfort, ambiance, and offering customers a relaxed space to work, socialize, or spend leisure time.

Why Choose a Café?

If your concept is built around affordable indulgence, day-time footfall, and repeat visits, a café might be your ideal format. Cafés are perfect for targeting younger audiences—college students, remote workers, and casual diners—who prefer relaxed environments and accessible pricing.

They also offer more flexibility in terms of timing and menu innovation. You can introduce seasonal beverages, curated snack menus, or even turn into a co-working space during slow hours. This model allows you to connect with your community in a meaningful, lifestyle-centric way.

If your goal is to build a branded space that becomes a local favorite, such as Third Wave Coffee or Blue Tokai cafés, this format allows you to achieve that without the massive CAPEX of a full-service restaurant.

Pros & Cons of Cafés:

Cafés typically have a lower barrier to entry. The startup cost ranges between ₹15–₹30 lakhs, depending on location and branding. They don’t require as much staffing or kitchen complexity as full-service outlets, making operations smoother and leaner.

They are also highly engaging social spaces. Customers tend to stay longer, return more frequently, and promote you through organic content on social media. With the right vibe, a café can become a cultural landmark in its neighborhood.

That said, revenues per customer are generally lower, which means you’ll need high footfall and frequent turnover to hit your targets. Cafés also face intense competition in urban markets. Without constant innovation—whether in décor, menu, or events—it’s easy to get lost in the crowd.

Location matters immensely. A well-run café in a dead zone won’t survive. You’ll need to invest smartly in finding high-footfall areas, ideally near colleges, office spaces, or residential communities.

QSR / Takeaway: 

Quick Service Restaurants (QSRs), also known as takeaways, are outlets that prioritize speed, affordability, and efficiency. The focus is on a limited menu, fast order delivery, and consistent quality.

Why Choose a QSR?

This model is ideal if you want to serve high-demand food categories—think pizza, wraps, rolls, biryani, momos, or fried chicken. If your product is designed for speed, mass appeal, and affordability, the QSR model helps you maximize volume while keeping operations tight.

QSRs are particularly attractive to those who want to build a franchise-ready brand. The processes are easy to replicate, and customer expectations are lower when it comes to ambience or service. Brands like WOW! Momo and Faasos have scaled rapidly using this format.

Pros & Cons of QSRs:

The primary advantage of QSRs is their scalability. Once your SOPs are dialed in, it’s easy to open new outlets across the city or even nationally. The operational model is lean, with fewer staff and smaller spaces—typically 200–500 sq. ft.

QSRs can also offer high margins on fast-moving products, especially when ingredient sourcing and prep is standardized. With a smart location (mall kiosk, high street, or tech park), footfall can be consistent all day.

The challenge with QSRs is that they’re heavily dependent on volume, which means your marketing, branding, and pricing need to be sharp from day one. You’re often competing with national chains, which means constant innovation and competitive pricing are required to stand out.

Customer loyalty can also be lower, especially if your food doesn’t wow on the first try. Consistency is key—one bad experience can push customers to try the next outlet down the road.

Cloud Kitchen: 

A cloud kitchen (also called a ghost or dark kitchen) is a delivery-only model. There is no dine-in or storefront presence. Orders are accepted and fulfilled exclusively through food delivery apps like Swiggy, Zomato, or your own website.

Why Choose a Cloud Kitchen?

Cloud kitchens are perfect for first-time entrepreneurs looking to test a food concept with minimal investment. They also suit businesses that want to scale multiple brands from a single kitchen—like a biryani brand, a momos brand, and a smoothie brand operating from the same location.

This format allows you to focus purely on food quality, packaging, and digital marketing, without worrying about the overheads of a physical outlet. It’s also ideal for targeting niche food segments like keto meals, vegan bowls, or regional home-style cuisine that thrive in delivery format.

Pros & Cons of Cloud Kitchens:

Cloud kitchens are cost-effective and fast to launch. A functional kitchen space, licenses, basic equipment, and a marketing budget can get you started for under ₹10 lakhs in many cities. There’s no need for prime-location real estate, expensive interiors, or service staff.

You also gain flexibility. You can tweak menus, test pricing, or pause operations with minimal loss. Plus, cloud kitchens allow you to leverage digital platforms to scale, making them ideal for tech-savvy entrepreneurs.

The biggest downside is visibility. Without a physical presence, you are entirely reliant on food delivery apps. Ranking high on Swiggy/Zomato requires aggressive marketing, paid promotions, and excellent reviews. Without this, it’s easy to get buried under competitors.

Also, brand-building is harder. Customers don’t walk in, experience your vibe, or interact with your staff. This makes it difficult to create emotional connections, which are essential for loyalty in the F&B space.

F&B Outlet Type Comparison Table (2025)

Outlet Type Estimated Investment (₹) Pros Cons
Full-Service Restaurant ₹50 lakhs – ₹1.5 crore Premium branding, higher bill value, immersive experience, customer loyalty High setup & operational cost, longer break-even period, staff-heavy operations
Café ₹20 lakhs – ₹40 lakhs Affordable entry, community-building, high footfall, good for social media marketing Lower margins per order, location-sensitive, needs constant innovation
QSR / Takeaway ₹15 lakhs – ₹35 lakhs Fast setup, scalable model, low rent, franchise-friendly Heavy competition, relies on volume, less customer connection
Cloud Kitchen ₹5 lakhs – ₹15 lakhs Lowest cost, fast launch, ideal for testing concepts, multiple brands in one kitchen No walk-ins, dependent on apps, hard to build emotional branding

How to Make the Right Outlet Choice

Before locking in your outlet type, take a step back and evaluate your business holistically. Some key factors to consider include:

1. Available Capital: Your budget determines the formats you can realistically pursue. Cloud kitchens and QSRs require a fraction of what full-service restaurants demand in setup and operational costs.

2. Target Audience & Food Category: Who are you serving, and what are you offering? A premium sushi menu may warrant a full-service experience, while affordable comfort food could thrive in a QSR or cloud kitchen model.

3. Operational Preference - Digital vs. In-Person: Do you prefer managing on-ground staff and guests, or focusing on digital channels and delivery metrics? Your comfort zone and team strengths matter more than you think.

4. Long-Term Vision: Are you building one flagship outlet, or do you see yourself scaling across cities? Cafés and QSRs are easier to replicate, while full-service restaurants build strong single-location brands.

If you’re starting small and want to validate your concept before scaling, a cloud kitchen offers the most flexibility. If your goal is to connect with customers and build a recognisable street presence, a café or QSR can help build visibility and daily sales. And if you're ready to go all in with a flagship experience, a full-service restaurant can help you create a legacy brand.

From fully-equipped cloud kitchens to prime café and restaurant outlets across Delhi NCR, Bangalore, Mumbai, and more—we’ve got verified listings and expert support every step of the way.

Whether you're launching your first outlet or scaling a proven concept, we help F&B businesses make strategic leasing decisions that lead to long-term success.

fields.name: How to Start a Cloud Kitchen from Home in India (2025) : A Complete Guide
fields.description:
It’s 2025, and food entrepreneurship has officially left the realm of big investments and fancy real estate. The biggest food brands popping up on your Swiggy and Zomato feeds today? Many of them started in someone’s 2BHK kitchen. This is the era of the cloud kitchen — and the best part? You don’t need to rent a commercial space to start one.

A cloud kitchen, also known as a ghost kitchen or delivery-only kitchen, is a food business that operates without a physical dine-in space. It relies entirely on digital orders through food delivery platforms like Swiggy, Zomato, and direct channels such as WhatsApp or Instagram. This model allows entrepreneurs to serve a wide customer base without the burden of high real estate investments, large teams, or elaborate storefronts.

The Indian cloud kitchen market was valued at $813 million in 2022 and is expected to cross $2 billion by 2026 (RedSeer, 2023). Combine that with a rising consumer appetite for fast, affordable, and high-quality delivery meals, and it’s clear: starting a cloud kitchen from home is no longer just a COVID-era workaround. It’s a viable, scalable business model — and one of the most exciting ways to enter the F&B space with minimal capital.

This guide walks you through everything you need to know about launching a cloud kitchen from your home — legally, practically, and profitably — specifically tailored for the Indian market.

1. Identify Your Niche 

Before starting your cloud kitchen, it’s important to clearly define what type of food you want to offer and who your customers will be. Look closely at your local delivery market on Swiggy and Zomato to spot popular cuisines and unmet needs. For example, if your area lacks quality vegan options or regional specialties like Bengali, Goan or North Eastern dishes, that’s an opportunity to stand out.

Think about what makes your kitchen different — whether it’s authentic recipes, affordable pricing, or fast delivery. A focused niche and clear unique selling point will help you attract customers in a crowded market. Doing this research early saves you time and effort later by ensuring there’s real demand for your offering.

2. Register Your Cloud Kitchen with FSSAI & Local Authorities

Operating a food business from home still requires compliance with government regulations. The most crucial step is securing your Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) registration. For startups expecting less than ₹12 lakh annual turnover, the Basic Registration is sufficient and can be completed quickly online via the FoSCoS portal.

If you anticipate higher turnover, you must apply for a State License, which entails stricter hygiene and operational checks. Additionally, check your local municipal corporation’s rules. Some cities require a trade license or kitchen hygiene certificate, especially if you live in gated communities or apartments with specific bylaws.

Starting with full compliance protects your business from legal troubles, builds credibility with customers, and is essential for onboarding on delivery platforms. Keep copies of all certificates handy to streamline platform registration.

3. Set Up a Functional & Compliant Kitchen at Home

Your home kitchen can be the heart of your cloud kitchen, but hygiene and efficiency are non-negotiable. Ensure clear separation of raw and cooked ingredients, and invest in durable, food-safe equipment such as stainless steel prep tables, sealed storage containers, and aprons.

Good ventilation and a commercial exhaust fan, if possible, improve food safety. Use gloves and hairnets during prep to meet hygiene standards. This setup won’t require heavy capital initially but must support quick, consistent food preparation while avoiding contamination risks.

Remember, platforms like Swiggy and Zomato may conduct random inspections, so visible hygiene practices help maintain your business reputation.

4. Build a Profitable & Delivery-Friendly Menu

Success depends heavily on your menu. Choose dishes that maintain quality after transit — avoid soggy or spill-prone items. Keep your menu tight, ideally 6 to 10 items, focusing on dishes that share ingredients to simplify prep and inventory management.

Calculate your food cost carefully, aiming to keep it within 30-35% of the selling price to ensure healthy margins. Offer consistent portion sizes and maintain quality to encourage repeat orders. Regularly analyze order patterns and customer feedback to refine your menu for better sales and operational efficiency.

5. Get Listed on Swiggy & Zomato 

Getting your cloud kitchen on Swiggy and Zomato is crucial for visibility and order volume. The onboarding process requires submitting your FSSAI registration, identity and address proofs, bank details, and finalized menu.

High-quality, appealing photos of your dishes are vital — invest in simple food photography that realistically showcases your offerings. Write detailed, engaging dish descriptions that highlight key ingredients, portion sizes, and unique features. Use keywords such as “homemade,” “fresh,” or regional specialties to improve searchability.

Define your delivery radius carefully, typically 5-6 km, balancing reach with food quality and delivery speed. Promptly accept orders and maintain a high acceptance rate, as this impacts your ranking within the app.

Actively monitor customer reviews. Respond professionally to criticism and thank satisfied customers. This engagement boosts your reputation and signals to the platform that you prioritize quality and service, increasing your visibility.

6. Invest in Professional Packaging & Kitchen Hygiene

In a delivery-only model, packaging is your brand’s first impression. Use tamper-proof, leak-resistant containers that keep food warm and intact during transit. Clearly label items to avoid confusion, and add thoughtful touches like reheating instructions or QR codes linking to feedback forms.

Behind the scenes, implement strict hygiene routines — daily cleaning, proper ingredient storage with FIFO (first in, first out), and temperature logs. These practices are critical not only for compliance but also for building trust with customers and delivery platforms.

7. Manage Orders & Delivery Smoothly

While Swiggy and Zomato handle delivery logistics, your role in ensuring smooth order fulfillment is vital. Make your kitchen easy to locate by providing clear addresses, landmarks, and any complex-specific instructions to help delivery partners.

Prepare orders in advance where possible and double-check every order for accuracy before handoff. Timely acceptance and preparation affect your app rankings, so stay attentive to notifications and avoid delays.

8. Promote Your Cloud Kitchen Through Instagram 

Trust is key for home-based food businesses. Instagram lets you connect visually with customers by sharing daily specials, behind-the-scenes kitchen stories, customer testimonials, and packaging details. Use features like Stories and Reels with local tags and trending audio to reach your neighborhood organically.

Besides Instagram, WhatsApp Business can help maintain repeat orders through broadcasts and personalized messaging. Google Business listings, hyperlocal ads on Meta (Facebook and Instagram), and partnerships with micro-influencers or local food bloggers can further amplify your reach.

While organic growth takes time, this foundation creates loyal customers and complements paid marketing efforts effectively.

9. Use Swiggy & Zomato Performance Marketing 

Listing your kitchen on food delivery apps is just the beginning. Swiggy and Zomato offer sophisticated marketing tools to increase your visibility and sales. Sponsored listings improve your placement in search results, promotional banners highlight your brand within categories, and discount campaigns attract first-time and repeat buyers.

These platforms also offer time-based boosts during peak hours and customer segmentation options to target specific groups like repeat customers or cart abandoners. Campaigns are measurable with real-time data on impressions, clicks, and returns.

However, many home chefs underutilize or overspend on these tools without strategic guidance. That’s where Broki comes in. We specialise in Swiggy and Zomato performance marketing — from campaign setup and targeting to daily optimization — helping you maximize visibility and returns on every rupee invested.

10. Know When & How to Scale Your Cloud Kitchen

When your monthly revenue reaches around ₹80,000 to ₹1.5 lakh, you may face capacity challenges — limited space, time, and energy. It’s time to consider scaling.

You can expand within your home by hiring kitchen staff and streamlining prep, or move to a dedicated cloud kitchen facility. These rentable spaces are available across major Indian cities, fully equipped with prep areas, delivery bays, and shared compliance infrastructure.

Scaling also opens up options like launching a second brand or enabling direct order fulfillment through your own website. Broki helps you find and rent cloud kitchen spaces in prime locations in top cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore and beyond, matching you with outlets that fit your cuisine and business needs.

Cloud kitchens have transformed food entrepreneurship in India. From a humble home kitchen, you can build a scalable, profitable brand serving thousands of customers without heavy upfront capital.

Success lies in a clear concept, legal compliance, smart menu design, and performance-driven marketing. When you’re ready to grow, Broki supports you — whether it’s finding the perfect kitchen space or running targeted Swiggy/Zomato ad campaigns that boost your revenue consistently.

Your first order could be the start of something much bigger!

fields.name: Things to Keep in Mind Before Leasing a Restaurant Property in India
fields.description:
Leasing the right property is one of the most crucial decisions when starting a restaurant business in India. Whether you’re launching a cloud kitchen, a QSR (Quick Service Restaurant), or a full-service dining experience, your location and lease terms will directly impact footfall, operations, and profitability.

At Broki.in, we’ve helped countless F&B entrepreneurs navigate the complexities of restaurant leasing in India. Here’s a detailed guide covering all the key factors you should keep in mind before signing that rental agreement.

Why Leasing the Right Restaurant Space Matters

In the Indian F&B industry, where margins are tight and competition is intense, your restaurant’s location and leasing terms can make or break your venture. High footfall zones, favorable lease agreements, and compliance with local regulations can give your business a competitive edge from day one.

Whether you're opening a new restaurant or expanding your brand, this blog walks you through what to check before leasing a restaurant property in India - so you avoid costly mistakes and start on solid ground.

1. Location Is Everything

The location of your restaurant is perhaps the most significant factor that will influence your success. A great concept in the wrong location can underperform, while a decent concept in the right spot can thrive. You need to assess whether the area attracts foot traffic from your target audience, whether it’s easily accessible by road or public transport, and if there are complementary businesses around such as offices, colleges, shopping areas, or nightlife zones. In metro cities like Bangalore, Mumbai, or Delhi, visibility and approachability are game changers. Before finalizing any property, conducting a thorough location feasibility study is highly recommended, which is something we at Broki.in help restaurant brands execute with data-backed precision.

2. Understand Your Target Audience

Not all areas are suitable for every restaurant concept. A fine-dining setup is unlikely to succeed in a college-dominated locality, just as a casual, budget café may not perform well in a premium shopping district. The demographic and spending habits of the people frequenting the location should align with your concept. Tools like Zomato and Swiggy insights, along with market research, can help you understand local consumption trends. This alignment between your brand and your audience is key to sustained footfall and loyalty.

3. Verify the Property’s Zoning & Licensing

One of the biggest mistakes new restaurant owners make is leasing spaces without ensuring they are zoned and approved for F&B operations. It’s essential to confirm that the property has all necessary licenses and approvals for restaurant use. This includes commercial zoning clearance, FSSAI eligibility, fire safety No Objection Certificate (NOC), and sanitation approvals. Without these, you may face delays, penalties, or even shutdowns. We always recommend verifying these details in advance—or better yet, let experts like Broki.in handle your licensing compliance to avoid legal complications.

4. Don’t Overextend on Rent

As a rule of thumb, your rent should ideally not exceed 10% to 15% of your projected monthly revenue. If your rent is disproportionately high, it will eat into your profits and create financial stress, especially during slow periods. In premium areas, negotiating a revenue-linked rental agreement can help de-risk your business. Understanding the rental trends in your city and negotiating effectively with landlords is a service we provide at Broki.in, ensuring you stay financially sustainable from day one.

5. Review the Lease Agreement Carefully

Lease agreements can contain several clauses that might affect your flexibility and finances. It’s important to carefully review the lock-in period, annual rent escalation terms, exit clauses, permissions for interior modifications, and sub-leasing rights. We strongly advise getting your lease vetted by a legal professional with experience in commercial F&B leases. At Broki.in, we help clients avoid traps hidden in fine print and negotiate favorable terms that support long-term growth.

6. Assess Power Load & Utilities

A fully functional restaurant requires more than just an attractive space—it needs proper infrastructure. You must ensure the property has adequate electrical load to support kitchen appliances, refrigeration, air conditioning, and lighting. Consistent water supply, drainage lines, and provisions for exhaust systems are also essential. Inadequate utilities can lead to operational delays or increased retrofitting costs. We assess such technical readiness during the site selection process to ensure you're not left with surprise expenses.

7. Scope for Renovation & Customization

Most restaurant properties will need interior and structural modifications to suit your brand identity and kitchen workflow. From installing kitchen exhaust systems to setting up drainage lines and custom lighting, every detail matters. Before you sign the lease, ensure that the landlord allows such changes and provides written consent. It’s also wise to budget for civil work, as design and compliance go hand in hand. Broki.in assists brands in managing these negotiations and planning compliant design changes.

8. Storage & Back-of-House Requirements

While dining areas are the face of the restaurant, the back-of-house operations drive its efficiency. Many first-time restaurateurs overlook the importance of adequate space for storage, dishwashing, staff restrooms, and waste disposal. A well-planned backend setup helps maintain hygiene, staff efficiency, and regulatory compliance. When evaluating a property, factor in the operational workflow and whether the layout can accommodate these essential functions smoothly.

9. Parking & Delivery Access

In India’s congested urban spaces, lack of parking can be a major turn-off for dine-in customers. Additionally, with food delivery becoming a major revenue stream, easy access for Swiggy and Zomato delivery partners is crucial. Ensure the property is accessible for two-wheelers, has space for quick pickups, and won’t lead to neighborhood disputes due to traffic or noise. Properties with dedicated loading/unloading zones can be a big plus.

10. Investigate the Property’s History

It’s worth knowing whether the property has previously housed a restaurant. If so, understanding why it shut down can reveal important insights—be it landlord issues, license problems, or customer complaints. You should also check for pending dues, unresolved legal matters, or structural maintenance issues like water leakage, pest infestation, or poor ventilation. A detailed property inspection can save you significant headaches down the line.

11. Confirm Building Compliance & Fire Safety

Fire safety is a non-negotiable element of any restaurant setup. The property must meet the building code and be equipped with the appropriate safety infrastructure. This includes fire exits, smoke detectors, extinguishers, and sprinkler systems. Obtaining a fire NOC is mandatory in most jurisdictions. Ignoring fire safety can lead to fines, closures, or worse—so always verify these elements before you invest in the space.

12. Choose a Landlord Who Understands the F&B Business

Finally, your relationship with the landlord can significantly affect your restaurant's day-to-day functioning. A landlord who has previously leased to restaurants will likely be more flexible about late-night operations, live music, outdoor signage, and renovation timelines. On the other hand, an inexperienced or difficult landlord can create obstacles and limit your ability to grow. At Broki.in, we help mediate between landlords and restaurateurs to ensure expectations are aligned and disputes are minimized.

Before you lease your restaurant space, remember that this is more than just a property deal—it's a strategic investment in your business's future. The right property can help you attract the right audience, streamline operations, and maximize profitability. Conversely, a poor leasing decision can drain resources, delay launch timelines, and hurt your brand’s reputation.

That’s why working with experienced F&B consultants like Broki.in can make a world of difference. Whether you're launching your first restaurant or expanding to a new market, our leasing experts help you secure the ideal space with confidence.

Closing isn’t as easy as shutting out the lights and closing the doors. There are calls to make, to notify sponsors, to address utilities and resources, and to keep workers updated and safe. Here are 5 important things you must keep in mind before closing a restaurant:

Inform your Team & Investors

The number one thing you need to do is sit down with your whole staff, let them know precisely what’s happening. You need to be transparent; you need to be clear, and you should be brief with telling them that they will be laid off for a while.

Regardless of whether they’ve been anticipating that you will close the bar or restaurant, listening to it out loud, and realizing that it’s going to happen, they’ll probably still be surprised and scared. Also, your providers and suppliers must know whatever decision you are taking. Start by setting the date that you will be shut and afterwards work in reverse. It is also essential to include the inventory check in the restaurant closing checklist. The closing manager should make a note in the checklist for vendor orders. fields.description:
Just Finished college or bored of your job, need to start something of your own, right?
Let’s open a restaurant.

Wait! Wait! Wait! Don’t hurry

Go through the key points that helps you opening up restaurant.

Concept or Cuisine:

Concept is the brain behind your restaurant and cuisine is the heart of the restaurant. They have to coordinate for the success of your restaurant.

How to choose a concept

  • If you are a creative person, brainstorm some concepts and write it down, or else find someone who is creative enough to help you in concept creation.
  • Alternatively, there are some concepts that are already running in some parts of the world but not in your city or country. Study those concepts and validate those from your friends and family.
  • Budget should be kept in mind while choosing the concept

Location:

First and foremost important thing is to find the perfect location. Bad location is slow poison that will eventually kill your business. A good location sets the mood of your restaurant. Good location does not always mean that is to be high street with high rentals, keep your budget in mind while choosing location.
How to choose location for restaurant

  • According to your rental budget, select areas that you want to explore.
  • Visit a restaurant that provides similar cuisine or concept and observe their footfall, talk to the staff, check menu and make some good observations on weekdays, weekends at lunch time, snack time and dinner time.
  • Too many restaurants serving your cuisine in that area is not a good indicator, step back. But, if your cuisine is familiar, then your taste, quality and service should be top notch
  • Choose a location that has a void that your cuisine or concept can fulfill
  • It should be a high density area

Site Selection

After you have finalize your area, its time for the perfect site

  • Visibility: The restaurant should be clearly visible from naked eyes, there should not be any hindrance or obstruction in the view of the restaurant and it should also be accessible
  • Size matters: Large size high rent, small size less rent. Choose the size according to your need, don’t get fascinated by large sizes, it will bleed our budget.
  • Dimension: Choose a site whose width is greater than or equal to its length.
  • Which Floor?: Ground floor is always preferable. However if there are upper floors, make sure there is a lift and should be working fine. Customers hate stairs.

Landlord Negotiation

Important things to keep in mind

  • Rental Amount: Negotiate the rental amount as much as you can, don’t be desperate for finalizing the deal if it’s not going as per plan don’t be shy away by walking off the deal. Chances will be high they will come back for the deal that suits you.
  • Security deposit: Try to keep it of lesser months so that your capital does not hurt
  • Lock-In period: Lock-in period is the duration in which lessee can’t leave the place, he has to pay the rent of that period irrespective of whether he is running the place or not. Try that there should be no or very less duration of the lock-in period.
  • Make sure that there is a Force majeure clause (unforeseeable circumstances that prevent someone from fulfilling a contract like a lockdown, the act of god, etc.) in the agreement

fields.name: All you want to know about a Cloud Kitchen
fields.description:
Cloud kitchen or the digital restaurant is the recent trend that has immediately settled itself in the F&B industry as a considerable successful restaurant format. With extreme competition in the restaurant space, high rentals, and increasing costs, Cloud Kitchen appears to be a more intelligent approach to maintain the restaurant business. With the surge of innovative tech hitting the restaurant business, we can guarantee you that the cloud kitchen trend is setting down deep roots, and would just develop different folds from here.

As per the research only 13% of the total market size has been tapped by cloud kitchens. This shows the immense potential this wonder-format holds. 

What is Cloud Kitchen concept? How does a Cloud Kitchen function?

Cloud kitchen is a place where food is prepared and delivered at door steps by accepting orders via calls and online ordering platforms. In contrast to other restaurants, they do not cater dine-in and takeaway. They exclusively put resources in food preparation and delivery or tie up with portals for food ordering such as Swiggy, Zomato etc. So it’s just a delivery-only restaurant, in a broader sense. 

Such commissary kitchens are often referred to as ghost kitchens, shared kitchens, or virtual kitchens with delivery-only food brands operating within them called virtual restaurants.

Now having known what it means, let’s see how a cloud kitchen functions.

Cloud kitchens are centralized licensed commercial food production facilities where anywhere from one or two to dozens of restaurants rent space to prepare delivery-optimized menu items. One restaurant may run multiple brands, or virtual restaurants, all operating under one roof, or the kitchen may be run like an incubator, shared by different purveyors. Picture a large warehouse with numerous stations (mini-restaurants) of stainless steel prep tables, hood vents, stoves, ovens, and sinks, each with its own orders coming in direct from customers. 

As the technology has matured, additional services have emerged to aggregate the various delivery apps into one portal, for easier production of multiple orders and delivery coordination as well as smart food purchasing and production software for decreased food waste and increased per meal unit economics. 

Cloud Kitchen Business Models

There are distinct approaches to running a cloud kitchen, ranging from adding an opportunistic delivery-only brand to an existing restaurant kitchen all the way to running a purpose-built commissary kitchen housing multiple brands. 

Let’s take a closer look at existing cloud kitchen business models.

1. The Independent/Standalone Cloud Kitchen

Single Brand, Single Kitchen, No Storefront

How it works

  • Online orders
  • Kitchens specialized in a cuisine
  • Delivery only
  • Self-delivery & via aggregators

2. The Multi-Brand Cloud Kitchen

Multi-brands (cuisine), a Shared Kitchen, Several outlets, no Storefront

How it works

  • Online orders
  • Kitchens specialized in a cuisine
  • Delivery only
  • Self-delivery & via aggregators

3. The Hybrid Cloud Kitchen

Single Brand, Shared Kitchen, Several Outlets, Storefront. 

How it works

  • Online orders
  • Single kitchens, single brand 
  • Multi cuisine seasonal menu
  • Delivery & take away
  • Self-delivery & via aggregators

4. Delivery app owned ‘Shell’ Cloud Kitchen

Aggregator operated, Multi (restaurant) brand, rented co-working kitchen, no storefront.

How it works

  • Online orders from owner delivery app
  • Multiple restaurant partner brands 
  • Restaurant brand rents bare shell space
  • Delivery via aggregators

5. Delivery app owned, fully stacked Cloud Kitchen

Aggregator operated, Multi brand (restaurant), rental kitchens, with a storefront. 

How it works

  • Online orders from owner delivery app
  • Multiple restaurant partner brands 
  • Restaurant just take care of the food
  • Customers have the option of walking in 
  • Delivery via aggregators

6. The fully outsourced Cloud Kitchen

Cooking & delivery fully outsourced.

How it works

  • Orders from all sources
  • The Cloud Kitchens buys & stores your raw materials
  • Then pre-prepares the food in its centralized kitchen
  • Sends it over to your kitchen for final touches
  • Picks it up & delivers it 

What’s behind the Cloud Kitchen trend?

The trend is driven by the coming of age of millennials with disposable income demanding digital, mobile-friendly solutions. Looking further forward, advances in kitchen automation, drone delivery, and the continued growth of the gig economy look to give cloud kitchens more of an advantage by lowering their costs even further.

Let’s take a closer look at the factors affecting the trend.

1. Real estate prices in urban areas

As urban real estate prices continue their upward trend, delivery-only kitchens are able to take advantage of their ‘virtual’ nature. The only restriction on their location is that they must be within a realistic delivery distance of enough hungry customers.

2. Increase in demand for delivery

Food delivery is set to grow to a $200 billion industry by 2025, due to shifting changes in behaviour, with nearly half of consumers preferring to eat at home. Consumers are increasingly willing to pay a significant amount for the convenience of having their food delivered.

3. Increase in on-demand contract workers 

With the gig or sharing economy in full swing, we’ve seen an increase in on-demand contract workers. The number of people working as ride-share drivers, delivery drivers, and remote workers is on the rise, offering low-cost labour with no strings attached from an employer’s point of view. But stability of the gig economy is still unknown. 

Emerging technologies decreasing the cost of delivery

Looking further forward, drone delivery and kitchen automation are set to disrupt the standard restaurant model further. Robot kitchens are on the rise and drone delivery is poised to break through, with only regional regulations standing in its way. 

Tech-minded shared kitchens are perfectly positioned to take advantage of these advances. They are much more able and likely to adapt quickly to new technology, giving them a further edge over storefront restaurants.

Are Cloud Kitchen profitable?

Cloud kitchen has been doing the rounds recently. The reason is that setting up a cloud kitchen does not require much investment and is easy to manage.

This is what happens exactly in a cloud kitchen model:

Orders come in, meals are prepared, packaged and then delivered to their distribution locations by the allocated fleet.

Why is this working?

Because you’re reducing the expense of your front-of-house operations and focusing on your food. With the introduction of third-party providers and the growing ease of online ordering, this concept seems to be perfect to start with. There are many more benefits to this Cloud Kitchen Business.

Benefits of Cloud Kitchens for Businesses

1. Reduced Real Estate & Operational Costs

Brick-and-mortar restaurants have to invest in real estate or physical location which is not the case with the cloud kitchen model. Since you’re removing table servicing out of the equation and offering a delivery-only service, Cloud kitchens get away with this additional cost, as they can be operated from any location including your home. Hence, no need to bear real estate expenses. Minimum staff is needed for this model and no-client facing staff is required, which also reduces the operational cost.

2. Better expansion opportunities & Scalable in Future

With a low investment sum, the cloud kitchen company will easily be scaled to other city regions. A single distributor can offer their services up to 2-3 miles away. You may also set up a wider kitchen outlet that provides food services across a wide area. 

The best part about cloud kitchens is you don’t need to make large expenditures. You can start small but expand rapidly. If you are building a reputation and having regular customers, it’s simpler to extend to other locations and even different menu range. 

Let’s take Faasos as an example, it operates 160 + kitchens and 4 brands today including Faasos, Behrouz Biryani, Oven Story and Firangi Bake.

3. Reduced Overhead Cost

Your profit margin is the fundamental motivation behind opening a cloud kitchen. You don’t need to pay for fancy doors and entrance, the client faced staff, and parking area. With a cloud kitchen, you save so much on overhead costs.

Your overall revenue is the primary reason for opening a cloud kitchen. You don’t have to pay for extravagant doors and entrance, the customer confronted staff, and parking region. With a cloud kitchen, you spare such a great amount on overhead expenses.

4. Cheaper advertising

Since cloud kitchens are exclusively online-based businesses, the most effective promoting channels for them is social media. With a brilliant social media approach, these restaurants can reach out to their target audience. These are more financially savvy when contrasted with conventional promoting like billboards, and can additionally help cut costs.

Here’s a list of some popular cloud kitchens start-ups in India

Faasos- Previously, a famous restaurant has now switched to a cloud kitchen, while some of the outlets still have some form of seating arrangement.

Behrouz Biryani- A biryani establishment serving a wide range of biryani.

Oven Story- Known for all their baked goods! Claims to have a secret ingredient that may or may not be grandma’s love!

Firangi Bake- They offer fusion dishes— Italian cuisine blended in with Indian Flavours.

Mandarin Oak- It’s about the celebration of peace, food and recipes that an amiable monk created under a loving oak tree which turned into his greatest motivation.

The Good Bowl- They are known to serve food from desi to fusion.

Box8- Known for its all-in-one meal boxes and fusion food boxes.

FreshMenu- They are famous for their frequent menu updates and offering gourmet meals.

Wrapping Up!

With the pace at which the F&B business is developing, cloud kitchens are the next major trend. While cloud kitchens entail low risk and high income, one should be cautious about the competition ahead to maximize income. There is no uncertainty that cloud kitchen would be the following major trend.

If you’re looking to grow your business or launch a food channel, cloud kitchen is the safer and wiser choice!

The cloud kitchen model presents a plenty of chances for both, the restaurateurs, and the aggregators and has additionally brought number of spin-off businesses that are sprouting in the F&B industry.
